script: Spread and total were not saved for Week 3 LAC@BUF, so this script is inferred only from the two-game form, not a posted number. Buffalo is the more stable offense: James Cook has 192 yards on 34 carries (5.65 YPC) and Josh Allen is +0.36 EPA vs blitz on 26 dropbacks and +0.63 without it. Justin Herbert is -0.86 EPA vs blitz on 14 dropbacks against Buffalo's 33% blitz rate, so Chargers drives are more likely to stall than to turn this into a shootout, with Omarion Hampton's 35 carries and 137 yards as the LAC answer if Herbert is under pressure.
who_goes_off: Dalton Kincaid is the one who should go off: 225 yards on 14 targets and 182 air yards (16.1 yards per target), and Josh Allen does not lose the blitz matchup at +0.36 EPA. James Cook's 96 rush yards per game is the carry volume, but LA has allowed 3.14 YPC and only 3 runs of 10-plus, so that 5.65 YPC does not travel. Ladd McConkey (117 yards on 10 targets) is the Chargers pass-catcher who can use Buffalo's 9.41 middle YPA, not Quentin Johnston, who has 24 yards on 11 targets.
weak_spot: Buffalo's weak spot is the middle of the field at 9.41 yards per attempt on 22 throws, versus 6.24 on the left (29 attempts) and 8.52 on the right (25), plus 9 passes of 20-plus on 83 attempts. LA's weak spot is the left side at 10.22 YPA on 27 attempts; the middle is a strength at 5.64 on 14 attempts, and the run front is the stingiest figure on the sheet at 3.14 YPC with 3 runs of 10-plus. No zone or man tag was saved, so the matchup read is these location splits, not outside corners.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for Week 3 LAC@BUF, so none of Dalton Kincaid's 14 targets or James Cook's 34 carries is being discounted for a lineup change. Usage is the two-game board only: Khalil Shakir 12 targets, DJ Moore 8 targets for 100 yards, Omarion Hampton 35 carries for 137 yards, Ladd McConkey 10 targets for 117 yards, Quentin Johnston 11 targets for 24 yards.
qb_vs_blitz: Justin Herbert is -0.86 EPA per dropback vs blitz on 14 snaps and +0.09 when not blitzed, and Buffalo blitzes 33%. Josh Allen is +0.36 EPA vs blitz on 26 dropbacks and +0.63 with no blitz, while LA blitzes only 25%. That is why Dalton Kincaid's 14 targets stay live and why Quentin Johnston's 103 air yards have produced only 24 receiving yards.

picks.why: Dalton Kincaid has 225 yards on 14 targets, 112.5 per game, and 182 air yards against a 57.5 line, so the number is about half his two-game rate. LA allows 10.22 YPA to the left on 27 attempts, and Josh Allen's +0.36 EPA vs blitz on 26 dropbacks faces only a 25% LA blitz rate, so those downfield targets are not getting taken away. LA's middle at 5.64 YPA on 14 attempts is a strength, but 13.0 air yards per target is not a checkdown diet that lives only between the hashes.

James Cook has 192 yards on 34 carries, 96 per game at 5.65 YPC, but LA has allowed 3.14 yards per carry and only 3 runs of 10-plus in two games. At his 17-carry rate, 3.14 YPC is about 53 yards, and he needs 4.74 YPC just to clear 80.5, a rate this run front has not surrendered. His 16 receiving yards on 7 targets are not in this rush market, so the under is the LA run-defense read, not a pass-game fade.
